messages:

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Remit routing & supplier ledger pathing — AP eligibility check

Hi Jordan & Asha,

Great speaking with you both earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can map the commercial path:

- Ask: Is SupplierLedger able to accept a Redwood PO (Net 30/60) or do you require payment by corporate card?
- Context: A few customers in your segment choose to pay via PO for accounting controls; others prefer card for speed. We need to know your AP gating (PO policies, payment terms, vendor onboarding SLA) to determine whether a marketplace install or a direct contract is the right route.
- Next steps: If PO is an option, can you confirm the exact billing entity name and whether 1099/W9 is required? If card is the only route, any corporate card limits (single txn or monthly) that would block initial pilot?

I've attached a short AP intake (fillable) and a draft SOW with pricing placeholders — returning the AP intake will help us flag any redlines early.

Attachments: SupplierLedger_AP_Form_Fillable.xlsx (fillable), SL_Onboarding_Terms_Draft.pdf (draft SOW).

Proposed timeline:
- You complete AP intake this week -> our finance ops triages (48h)
- If PO: we send contract + routing steps -> expected vendor setup 5–7 business days
- If card/marketplace: we can enable pilot within 24–48 hours after PO/card confirmation

Would you prefer a short follow-up call tomorrow to run through the AP form?

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0147
E: tessa@redwood.ai

Redwood Inference | Production-first inference for product teams
From: Jordan Hale <jh@supplierledger.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@supplierledger.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Remit routing & supplier ledger pathing — AP eligibility check

Thanks Tessa — good call. Asha and I chatted after; quick answers so you can triage:

- Our AP team prefers PO for anything over $5k and standard terms are Net 60.
- We can accept card for pilots <$5k but our corporate card is limited to $3k per transaction (procurement card).
- Marketplace installs are attractive because they simplify procurement approvals, but they require that the provider be listed on our procurement marketplace (we're not sure Redwood is currently listed).

We're going to fill the AP intake you attached and return it by EOD tomorrow. Two clarifying Qs:
1) If PO is needed, does Redwood have a standard vendor packet (bank details, tax form) we can attach to the PO?
2) If marketplace is required, what is the typical onboarding time to get Redwood listed?

Appreciate it — Jordan

Jordan Hale
VP Partnerships, SupplierLedger
jh@supplierledger.com
From: tessa_morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hale <jh@supplierledger.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@supplierledger.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Remit routing & supplier ledger pathing — AP eligibility check

Jordan — perfect, thanks for the quick answers. Short replies to your Qs and notes: 

1) Vendor packet: Yes — we can provide vendor packet (bank details, Redwood W9, certificate of insurance). I'll attach a vendor packet PDF in a follow-up. For PO routing we typically need entity legal name, remit address, and a PO contact.

2) Marketplace listing: Typical time to be listed depends on the marketplace operator — 2–6 weeks on average (due diligence + contract addendum). If Marketplace is mandatory for you, we can start the paperwork in parallel but pilot timing may be delayed.

Two asks for AP triage:
- Please confirm billing/legal entity exactly as it should appear on a PO.
- If Net 60 is non-negotiable, call that out so we can align finance.

I'll also loop in our finance ops directly (monica) to accelerate vendor setup once we have the intake back. If you want to expedite, we can accept an initial card payment for the pilot while PO is processed.

Thanks — I'll wait for the filled intake.

Best,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@supplierledger.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Remit routing & supplier ledger pathing — AP eligibility check

Thanks — attached is our AP intake (completed) and a short AP policy excerpt that flags vendors requiring a marketplace listing for anything affecting our product ledger. Key points:

- Billing entity: SupplierLedger, Inc. (EIN: XX-XXXXXXX)
- Net terms: Net 60 standard, must be honored for any contract >$5k
- Card use: Procurement card allowed for pilots < $3k only
- Marketplace: Required for vendors that will touch our secure product data (our legal team flags this).

We've attached the intake and policy excerpt. If Redwood can provide the vendor packet and W9 today, we'll start the PO flow. If Marketplace is necessary, we'll need to know whether Redwood supports the required security attestation for listing.

Attachments: SupplierLedger_AP_Intake_0427.xlsx, SL_AP_Policy_Excerpt.pdf

-Asha

Subject: Internal: next steps on SupplierLedger AP routing

Tessa — quick internal summary and recommended playbook: 

- They require Net 60 for >$5k and marketplace for vendors touching product data. Pilot under $3k allowed by card, but single-transaction cap.
- Ask finance to prepare vendor packet + W9 and flag the PO flow (we can pre-seed bank details). Monica to run vendor creation once we receive the intake.
- Parallel path: Offer an initial card-paid pilot <$3k to unblock product evaluation while legal/marketplace work proceeds. Document: send a short 'pilot payment' acceptance email template.

I'll draft the vendor packet and send to Asha within the hour. Monica, can you confirm vendor setup SLA (business days) and whether we can expedite on our side?

Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
